name: Lakuramau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Mazzitelli, Lidia. 2021. A Grammar of Lakurumau. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (paywalled). Her open-access LD&C 14 (2020) article was read: phonology sketch has no stress statement.
earlier_scan.note: Full grammar's phonology chapter is the place to look; De Gruyter access blocked.

sources.citation: Mazzitelli, Lidia Federica. 2020. Documentation of Lakurumau: Making the case for one more language in Papua New Guinea. Language Documentation & Conservation 14: 215-237. http://hdl.handle.net/10125/24922
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Section 3.1 (pp. 226-227) gives 6 vowels, 16 consonants and lenition rules; fn. 8 p. 226: 'This is only a sketch of the Lakurumau phonology; I plan to write a more detailed account of Lakurumau phonetics and phonology in the future.' No stress statement. Implicit evidence only: Table 5 p. 227 transcriptions faazak [ˈfazək] / vazaak [vəˈzak], kaabang [ˈkabəŋ] / xabong [ɣəˈbɔŋ], paala [ˈpalə] / valai [vəˈləi] place stress on the full vowel /a/ <aa> rather than on schwa /ə/ <a>, in whichever syllable it sits.

sources.citation: Mazzitelli, Lidia Federica. 2023. Describing contact-induced language changes: how to avoid stigmatising speakers? ICLDC 8 poster abstract. https://hdl.handle.net/10125/104850
